title: Command Injection Vulnerability in MCP STDIO Transport
notes: Fixed by adding validateStdioCommand() that checks for shell metacharacters and validates command paths
close_reason: All security fixes implemented and verified. All tests passing.

title: Path Traversal Vulnerability in Agent File Operations
notes: Fixed by using filepath.EvalSymlinks to properly resolve symlinks and added Windows UNC path and drive letter validation

title: Integration tests overwrite the developer's REAL ~/.chatgpt-cli/config.yaml
description: test/integration/integration_test.go builds config paths from path.Join(os.Getenv("HOME"), ".chatgpt-cli"). On Windows HOME=C:\Users\david, so running 'go test -run Integration' silently destroys the developer's live config.yaml (observed 2026-09-19: real config replaced with model: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 / thread: thread-name / max_tokens: 789, causing a 404 on the next real 'gpt' invocation). Tests assert Expect(configFile).NotTo(BeAnExistingFile()), which assumes a throwaway HOME. Fix: point the suite at a t.TempDir()/OPENAI_CONFIG_HOME sandbox instead of HOME.
close_reason: Root cause: os.UserHomeDir() reads USERPROFILE on Windows, not HOME. The suite sandboxed only HOME, so the spawned CLI wrote to the developer's real profile. Now sets and restores both. Also fixed: hardcoded port 8080 (Windows allows a second bind over an existing listener -> connection races) replaced with an OS-assigned ephemeral port; POSIX-only path/error-string assertions made platform-neutral. Integration suite on Windows: 29 failures -> 0.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure via Insecure File Permissions
notes: Fixed by changing all sensitive file writes from 0644 to 0600 in history/store.go, config/store.go, cmd/chatgpt/utils/utils.go, and cmd/chatgpt/main.go
close_reason: All security fixes implemented and verified. All tests passing.

title: Unvalidated User Input in Shell Command Arguments
notes: Fixed by adding checks for shell variable expansion ($, `, %), glob patterns (*, ?, [), and tilde expansion anywhere in arguments
close_reason: All security fixes implemented and verified. All tests passing.

title: pre-commit hook fix is machine-local and will regress on any fresh clone
description: The bd pre-commit hook called 'bd sync --flush-only', a flag removed from current bd, so EVERY commit failed with 'Failed to flush bd changes to JSONL'. Fixed 2026-09-19 to use 'bd export -o $BEADS_DIR/issues.jsonl'. But core.hooksPath is unset and .git/hooks is untracked, so the fix exists only on this workstation. A fresh clone, or a bd reinstall that rewrites the hook, reintroduces a total commit block. Fix: add a tracked .githooks/ dir and set core.hooksPath, or pin the bd version.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Prepared and verified, but NOT closeable by me - the last step is a commit (see bottom).

WHAT I DID:
- Created tracked .githooks/ holding BOTH hooks, byte-identical copies of the working ones in .git/hooks (verified with cmp): pre-commit AND post-merge.
  ⚠️ post-merge matters: core.hooksPath REPLACES .git/hooks wholesale, so moving only pre-commit would have silently killed the post-merge beads import. That is a trap this fix had to avoid, not a bonus.
- Added .githooks/README.md explaining why the hooks live in git, how to enable them, and the wholesale-replacement caveat for anyone adding a hook later.
- Added a 'make hooks' target (Makefile) that runs 'git config core.hooksPath .githooks' and echoes the result back. core.hooksPath is LOCAL git config and cannot be set from inside a repo (git refuses, by design, so a clone cannot run code on checkout), so a fresh clone genuinely needs one command - that is the irreducible part, and 'make hooks' is it.
- Ran it: core.hooksPath = .githooks.

VERIFIED:
- 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' now answers '.githooks', so git really is resolving hooks from the tracked dir.
- 'sh .githooks/pre-commit' exits 0 and stages .beads/issues.jsonl as designed. (I then restored the index to how I found it, since I am not committing.)
- The bead's premise re-confirmed: 'bd sync --flush-only' answers 'Error: unknown flag: --flush-only', so the pre-fix hook did block every commit.
- Repo has one tracked Makefile (the second 'makefile' listing is the same file on case-insensitive NTFS), so the target is not duplicated.

⚠️ WHY THIS IS STILL OPEN: the entire point of the bead is that the fix must survive a FRESH CLONE, and .githooks/ is currently UNTRACKED. Until it is committed, the fix is exactly as machine-local as the one it replaces. I have no instruction to commit, so I did not.

ONE COMMAND FROM DONE:
  git add .githooks Makefile && git commit -m 'fix(hooks): track hooks in .githooks and add make hooks bootstrap (beads-dvf)'
Then on any fresh clone: 'make hooks'.

Working tree also carries .golangci.yml (beads-9yz, closed) and a .beads/config.yaml change (beads-9i3, left open with findings).

title: Add .golangci.yml pinning max-same-issues: 0 so the gate cannot hide work
description: golangci-lint defaults to max-same-issues=3, which TRUNCATES repeated findings. A first pass reported 20 issues; clearing them revealed 8 more of the same shape that had been suppressed. The repo has no .golangci.yml, so CI inherits the truncating default and its reported count understates the real backlog. Fix: commit a .golangci.yml with max-same-issues: 0 and max-issues-per-linter: 0.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Added .golangci.yml with max-same-issues: 0 and max-issues-per-linter: 0.

SCHEMA NOTE: golangci-lint here is v2 (local 2.13.2; CI uses golangci-lint-action with version: latest, so also v2), whose config schema differs from v1 - the file carries 'version: "2"'. Validated with the tool's own checker: 'golangci-lint config verify' exits 0. Linter SELECTION is left at the default set on purpose; this file is about the completeness of the report, not about changing what is linted.

MEASURED, because the current tree is lint-clean and therefore cannot show the effect (both configs report '0 issues' on it). I added a temporary 6-function probe package with six ineffassign findings of the same shape, ran it both ways, and deleted it:
  with .golangci.yml            -> 6 issues (ineffassign: 6)
  with --max-same-issues=3      -> 3 issues (ineffassign: 3)
That is the truncation this bead describes, reproduced and removed. (First probe attempt did not compile - 'declared and not used' is a Go compile error, so no linters ran at all and both runs reported 0; a probe that produces no findings proves nothing either way, so it was corrected to return the variable.)

NOT COMMITTED - no explicit instruction to commit. Untracked: .golangci.yml.

title: New beads get the 'beads-' prefix instead of 'chatgpt-cli-'
description: Issues created before the SQLite->Dolt migration use the chatgpt-cli-* prefix (chatgpt-cli-699, -bib, -2tw...); issues created after it use beads-* (chatgpt-cli-c2525126, chatgpt-cli-0368d55f, chatgpt-cli-5fc730e0). issue-prefix is commented out in .beads/config.yaml in BOTH the old and new versions, so this is not config regression - the old prefix came from the retired SQLite DB. Cosmetic, but IDs are now inconsistent. Fix: set issue-prefix: chatgpt-cli in .beads/config.yaml.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
INVESTIGATED - NOT CLOSED. The prescribed fix does not work, and the fix that does has a side effect worth your decision.

1. THE PRESCRIBED FIX IS INSUFFICIENT. I set 'issue-prefix: "chatgpt-cli"' in .beads/config.yaml (it is now set, replacing the commented-out line), then TESTED it by creating a throwaway bead: it came back 'beads-k8n', still the wrong prefix. Probe deleted immediately. The config file's own comment is accurate - 'Issue prefix for this repository (used by bd init)' - so it only applies at init time and has no effect on an existing Dolt DB. Left the setting in place because it is correct for a future re-init, but on its own it changes nothing about this bead's symptom.

2. THE REAL MECHANISM is 'bd rename-prefix chatgpt-cli- --repair', which is purpose-built for exactly this ('Consolidating multiple prefixes after database corruption'). Current state: 13 issues = 7 chatgpt-cli-* + 6 beads-*.

3. ⚠️ BUT THE DRY RUN SHOWS A TRADE-OFF THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE. It would rename to 8-char hex suffixes, not the short IDs the existing issues use:
     beads-dvf -> chatgpt-cli-ee89fa1d
     beads-9yz -> chatgpt-cli-8247acf1
     beads-9i3 -> chatgpt-cli-17a86386   (this bead)
   Existing IDs are chatgpt-cli-699 / -bib / -2tw. So it makes the PREFIX consistent while making the ID FORMAT inconsistent. For a P3 cosmetic bead that is a judgement call, not an obvious win, so I did not run it.

SAFETY CHECKED: no git commit messages and no markdown docs reference any beads-* ID, so a rename would not strand outside references. The operation is local to the Dolt DB. '--dry-run' is available for re-checking.

YOUR CALL: (a) run the repair and accept mixed ID formats, (b) leave the prefixes mixed, or (c) rename and separately normalise the old short IDs. Say which and it is a one-command change.

NOT COMMITTED. Working tree carries .beads/config.yaml (issue-prefix set) and the .golangci.yml from beads-9yz.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
FIXED via 'bd rename-prefix chatgpt-cli- --repair' (owner-approved 2026-09-19).

RESULT: 6 issues renamed, 7 unchanged, 13/13 now chatgpt-cli-*. No beads-* remain.
  beads-dvf -> chatgpt-cli-ee89fa1d   (tracked-hooks bead, still open)
  beads-n39 -> chatgpt-cli-c2525126
  beads-3l9 -> chatgpt-cli-5fc730e0
  beads-9yz -> chatgpt-cli-8247acf1   (golangci config, closed)
  beads-9i3 -> chatgpt-cli-17a86386   (this bead)
  beads-58a -> chatgpt-cli-0368d55f

⚠️ VERIFIED THE ACTUAL SYMPTOM, not just the rename. This bead was about NEW issues getting the wrong prefix, and the originally-prescribed fix (issue-prefix in .beads/config.yaml) did NOT change that - proven earlier with a throwaway bead that still came back 'beads-k8n'. So I re-tested after the repair: created a throwaway -> 'chatgpt-cli-f5r', correct prefix. Probe deleted.

BETTER THAN THE DRY RUN SUGGESTED: new IDs come out SHORT ('f5r'), not the 8-char hex. The hex form applies only to the six renamed historical rows, so the format inconsistency is bounded and does not grow. That was the one reservation raised before approval.

The .beads/config.yaml 'issue-prefix: "chatgpt-cli"' setting added earlier is retained - it is correct for a future re-init, though it was not what fixed this.

SAFETY (re-confirmed pre-rename): no git commit messages and no markdown docs referenced any beads-* ID, so nothing outside the tracker was stranded.
